notes: 22 mm TPU heel on a light chassis. Flexes enough at the toe for the back foot in a split jerk, and stays put in the catch. Fit runs on the narrow side.
20 mm heel with the TPU power bridge back around the midfoot, plus two straps. Very planted. Wide feet should try it on first.
The classic from the 2012 London Olympics. ¾-inch TPU heel, two straps, and two insoles in the box: a softer one for training and a hard one for meets. Still sold as new old stock in a few shops.
Lü Xiaojun's own lifter. The TPU heel is graded by size from 24.5 to 27 mm, the tallest here. Microfiber upper, and a thinner spare insole comes in the box if the fit runs tight.
22 mm TPU heel with an external heel clip and the inflatable Pump tongue. Very stiff platform. RunRepeat weighed it as the heaviest lifter in their lab.
21 mm drop, rigid TPU midsole and a patented wide toe box. The first one to try if Nike or Adidas crush your toes. TYR suggests a half size up.
The original wide-toe-box lifter with a 21 mm drop. Superseded by the L-2, so it often shows up discounted.
TYR's top lifter: carbon construction, a 21 mm drop, leather upper and a wide fit. List price is $350, but it has been on deep sale.
The first lifter Rogue ever sold, brought back with a stacked genuine-leather heel. The drop is graded by size, about 19 mm in the middle sizes.
15 to 16 mm heel on high-density EVA, so it compresses a little under heavy loads. A good first pair, or a squat shoe for powerlifters.
Nike's entry lifter with a 15 mm heel and a flexible forefoot. Fine for learning the lifts; the low heel can feel off if you're used to Romaleos.
Zero drop and maximum ground feel. Some deadlifters swear by it; for the snatch and clean you lose the heel that helps you sit upright in the bottom.
Rogue's long-running budget lifter: a ¾-inch plastic heel, two metatarsal straps and a wide profile that suits wide feet.
The previous Legacy: 22 mm TPU heel, one wide strap and a reworked toe box. RunRepeat weighed it at 612 g. Easy to find on sale now that the III is out.
Nike went light: Flywire mesh upper, one big midfoot strap and a honeycomb TPU heel, about 380 g with the soft insole. Narrow fit, and the original mesh upper had durability complaints.
The 2019 Extra Durability fix for the Romaleos 3: perforated leather instead of mesh, a beefier strap, same 20 mm honeycomb heel. Listed at $200 when it was current.

Lu's old-school lifter: solid beechwood heel, genuine leather upper and Goodyear-welted construction. Slightly lower heel than the PowerPro and the classic wood-heel slap. Limited runs in white and pink.
The second-generation Elite Carbon: a dense wooden heel over a full-length carbon-fiber POWERPLATE, perforated leather upper and a double-strap lockdown. TYR hasn't published the heel height yet.
The 2012-era original with a leather upper, Torsion bar and a 20.1 mm TPU heel. Many lifters still call it the best Adidas lifter ever made.
2019 redesign with a woven textile upper and the same 20.1 mm TPU heel as the original. Lighter and more breathable, but softer and more flexible than the OG.
The 1-inch heel Adidas: a BOA dial instead of laces and straps, a woven upper and a tall TPU wedge. Loved by high-bar squatters with tight ankles.
The budget canvas lifter before the Powerlift 5: a 15 mm high-density EVA wedge and one strap. A gentle first step up from flat shoes.
Beijing-era flagship: polished wood heel, glossy leather and a chrome Torsion shank. The last Adidas lifter with a wood heel and a collector's grail today. Runs about a size big.
Adidas' 2008 training lifter: an exposed wooden heel wedge, perforated synthetic-leather upper and a single hook-and-loop instep strap.
Handmade in Japan and basically unchanged for decades: suede or leather upper, staggered lacing, no strap, and a solid wood heel nailed to a rubber sole. Hard to buy outside Japan.
The original Romaleo built for the 2008 Beijing Olympics. Heel height scaled with shoe size, and it weighed about 620 g, roughly a quarter more than the Romaleos 2.
Reebok's first true weightlifting shoe, made with CJ Cummings in 2017: 22 mm TPU heel 82 mm wide, an Exoframe heel clip and two straps. The Legacy Lifter 2 dropped to one strap.
Reebok's 2026 lifter: a 33 mm TPU heel clip, a wide Evo midfoot strap that Reebok says holds with twice the force, and a padded collar. Reebok hasn't published the heel drop yet.
A budget lifter with a 15 mm high-density EVA heel and a breathable textile upper. A good first pair or a hybrid shoe. Heavy lifters may want a firmer heel.
The 2024 update to Reebok's budget lifter. The drop goes up to 18 mm and the price stays around $100. Light enough to wear for a whole class.
Named for its weight of 360 g. It has a TPU POWERTRUSS heel cage under a 16.5 mm drop and a flexible forefoot, so it also works as a hybrid shoe on CrossFit days. Slim fit.
Handmade with a stacked leather heel and a SuperFabric upper. It sold for $299, but NOBULL's site no longer lists it, so look for used pairs.
Adidas's budget lifter. It has a high-density die-cut wedge with a ¾-inch heel, a synthetic leather upper and a strap that sits high, near the ankle. Tough and cheap.
A modern lifter with a real wooden heel (22 mm), from a small Minnesota brand. Reviewers love the crack of wood on the platform. It runs small and narrow, so size up.
Handmade in California with a hand-carved, stained wood heel a full inch tall, one of the tallest you can buy. Suede upper with one wide strap.
The shoe ANTA makes for China's national weightlifting team, sold abroad without the flag. It has a 20 mm TPU heel, two straps and a heavy, leather-style upper. Shops compare it to the Romaleos 2.
LUXIAOJUN's first lifter, before the PowerPro. It has a 20 mm TPU heel (95 Shore A) and two straps, and the inside is roomy. You can still find leftover stock.
